title: Yomikata entry: how to read one game release's text

id.description: The release's id (PS1/PS2 serial SLPS-01234, PSP DISC_ID ULJM06119, DS game code AXXJ, 3DS product code CTR-P-XXXJ, GameCube GXXJ01). The file is games/<platform>/<id>.json.

aliases.description: Other ids of the same release that share this entry, e.g. the serials of discs 2+ of a multi-disc game.

title.description: The title as printed on the release (Japanese where it has one).

versions.description: Releases this entry is known to fit: hash of the boot executable (discs) or of the header (cartridges).

id.description: Which id (main or alias) this hash belongs to; default: the main id.

tables.description: Thingy .tbl files applied in order (later ones win). Keys are hex in memory byte order.

unit.description: Bytes per character code for table decoding.

controls.description: Control codes (hex, memory byte order) and what they mean.

cleanup.description: Declarative text cleanup, applied in order: regex replacements and character remaps.

hooks.description: Code addresses each line passes through (PSP via PPSSPP's debugger, for now).

versions.description: exe_sha1 values this hook was confirmed on; empty = all listed versions.

layouts.description: Where the game keeps what it shows, for readers that read memory instead of hooking. Every field is optional: a partial layout (just the message) is still useful.

versions.description: exe_sha1 values this layout was confirmed on; empty = all listed versions.

endian.description: Of pointers and numbers. Default little (GameCube/Wii: big).

poll.description: How often reading is enough: every frame, or a rate in Hz.

message.description: The text the message window shows (whole, even while it types out).

speaker.description: Who speaks: the name as text, or a number (see speaker_names).

speaker_names.description: Number -> the name as shown, for games whose name plate is a picture. Names only.

shown.description: How many characters of the message are on screen yet.

waiting.description: Flag: the line is complete and the game waits for a press.

choice_cursor.description: Which answer (from 0) the cursor is on.

when.description: Flag: the addresses hold what the layout says. While it is false nothing else is read: texts are empty, flags false, numbers left out.

by.description: Number: which set is loaded now.

sets.description: The number's value (decimal) -> table files applied after the entry's.

tables.description: For a game that numbers its characters anew per chapter: the table files that follow the entry's tables, chosen by a number in memory. No set for the number: table texts can't be read.

status.description: verified: a person confirmed it in play. auto: built by the pipeline and passed validation. partial: known gaps.

where.description: A fixed address, or a pointer chain: start at base; for each offset, read the pointer there and add the offset.

equals.description: For flags: true when the value equals this (default: true when nonzero).

mask.description: For flags: only these bits of the value count, for nonzero and for equals.

counts.description: What the number counts. Default bytes.

charset.description: table: the entry's tables, unit and controls.

max_bytes.description: Never read more than this (per row, with rows).

terminator.description: Hex in memory byte order, checked at character boundaries: 00, 0000, FFFF.

length.description: The text's length (each row's, with rows), read from memory.

lengths.description: One length per row, the numbers one after another in memory.

rows.description: Rows stride bytes apart, each read to its terminator, its length or the stride, joined with newlines.

break.description: The code between two pages, hex in memory byte order, checked at character boundaries: 0C.

type.description: Default u8; a pointer is u32.

cursor.description: Number: the address in the text the game is reading at.

pages.description: For a buffer holding several pages of script: the text is the page the game's cursor is on. Not with rows.

open.description: The code a text starts after, hex in memory byte order: 8000. Without it the script is one text from its start.

counts.description: What the number counts: bytes, or codes of `unit` bytes. Default bytes.

offset.description: Number: how far past the text's address the game is reading.

texts.description: Each text of the page is a row of its own: a list the game writes as one text per item, such as a choice's answers.

rest.description: How many codes past a text's end code the game may stop while the text stays up: a position that far past one is read as just past it.

script.description: For a game that reads its text straight out of a script with instructions in it: the address is the script's start, and the text is the page the game is reading, as far as it has read. A page code inside a text starts the page anew. Only with a table charset; not with rows, pages, terminator or length.

codes.description: Codes in the text that aren't characters: the bytes a code starts with (hex in memory byte order), and how many bytes it has in all, those included. {"07": 2} is 07 and one argument byte. A code is skipped whole, so its arguments are never taken for the terminator or for text. With a table charset: the controls that take arguments.

when.description: Flag: the text is on screen. While it is false the text is empty, whatever the memory holds.
